A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UniRestorer. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original restoration results, generalization experiments, ablations, and supplementary routing and computational-cost analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains original restoration and supplementary experimental results and adds a degradation-representation visualization in Figure B.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 changes the reported hierarchy construction: v2 starts with finest-level clusters and clusters their centers upward, whereas v3 recursively partitions sample groups from coarse to fine. This revises an existing construction stage; expert backbones, losses, and dual-router restoration remain intact.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same seven single-degradation tasks, mixed-degradation scenarios, real-world datasets, and unseen-corruption evaluations. The unseen-corruption table moves into the main text; the new feature visualization uses already represented degradation types.

E2.justification: Table 1 substantially expands the quantitative comparator set with DaAIR and MoCEIR under both 3T and 5T settings, PromptIR-TUR-3T, Transweather-TUR-5T, and DCPT-PromptIR-5T. Existing comparators are retained.

E3.justification: Real-world evaluation reporting changes from PSNR and SSIM in v2 Table 8 to PSNR alone in v3 Table 4. The extractor ablation is described using multigranularity partitions in v3 Appendix B, replacing v2 Appendix D's explicit four-cluster description. Its unchanged scores do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds Figure B's t-SNE analysis comparing degradation separability in Restormer, PromptIR, and UniRestorer representations. Existing extractor, granularity, routing, loss, lightweight-expert, and scaling analyses remain, although several move or receive new labels.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The retained granularity-uncertainty mechanism and expert-usage statistics do not constitute changed experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v3 adds baseline result entries in Table 1, including DaAIR-3T dehazing at 32.30 dB and MoCEIR-5T deblurring at 30.05 dB, plus Figure B's separability findings. It removes real-world SSIM entries. Retained UniRestorer scores and the existing qualitative restoration comparisons are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 and Equation 6 correct the hierarchy's index range from 0 through n to 0 through n-1 while retaining n=3. This resolves the inconsistency between the stated number of levels and their formal indexing. No new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims: multigranularity restoration mitigates degradation-estimation errors, outperforms existing all-in-one methods, and closes the gap to single-task models. The revised contribution bullets reorganize these claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations connecting baseline limitations to poorly separated degradation features and prompt misidentification. It explains the RetinexFormer choice through Restormer's low-light weakness and discusses compatibility with efficient expert designs such as LoRA. Existing data-scale and real-world coverage limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 expands the DA-CLIP controller and feature-alignment description and clarifies granularity-level load balancing. It removes the explicit BLIP caption-generation disclosure and detailed per-task allocation of finest-level experts. Optimizer settings, hardware, and the promise of future code/model release remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds the works supporting DCPT, task uncertainty regularization, and MoCEIR. Section 3.2 more explicitly positions the expert architecture relative to GRIDS, RestoreAgent, and efficient fine-tuning. The broader related-work taxonomy and novelty positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: The introduction, contribution list, experimental setup, and several discussions are extensively rewritten. The appendix substantially reorganizes data, implementation, expert-design, and routing material into consolidated sections and adds a Broader Impacts section.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout, extensively resizing and relocating displays. Unseen-corruption results move into the main text, router ablations move to the appendix, Figure B is added, and Figures 1 and 3 are revised. Existing appendix restoration images are retained but resized.

improvement.justification: The added Table 1 baselines, Figure B diagnostics, and clearer organization strengthen comparative support and explanation. However, removing real-world SSIM also removes evidence favoring InstructIR on LHP and LOLv2 in v2 Table 8. Section 3.2 reverses the clustering prescription without clarifying its relationship to the unchanged restoration results, and some reproducibility details disappear. These benefits and losses leave the net quality direction uncertain.
